task.description: WF-02 step 1b gate, CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, the M2.3 design for REQ-116 and REQ-117. Apply your whole checklist: every criterion (22) leads to a design element and a named test; no «decide later»; signatures, data, codes and errors complete; bar section complete; protection in the same operation as the action — look hard at: the plan-before-switchToTenant audit append (one transaction, platform first, no way back), the invite one-time use and its token storage, acceptance creating user + membership + consent + audit atomically, the idea version number under concurrency (row lock), the purge protocol app.purge_org and who can set it, the users guard trigger, RLS on the four new tables, grants.sql additions, the consent sentences and the narrow word-list exception, deletion; no contradiction with decisions or the released code; no implementation code. Repeat the design's claims about today's code YOURSELF on a fresh clone of the tag base/M2PROJ-20261124-01 under <scratch> (npm ci in app/; PGlite; your own scripts only, never the repository test suites, npm run check or e2e: decision 0110); apply at least 12 of the design's mutants to a sketch and say which test kills each; check the replacement table (26 rows) against a search of app/test and tools/test; assess the sub-steps. PASS or FAIL, findings by severity with the exact change wanted. Be thorough: invitations and consent are the first personal-data path of the product. RULES OF THIS PC (decisions/0110, 0127, 0129): do NOT run npm run check, cd app && npm run ..., node --test, the tools test scripts or the e2e tests; the record of a test run is read from GitHub with gh run view (read-only). Allowed: cd tools && npm run -s traces and handoffs-check; read-only git and gh; your own scripts and fresh clones (git clone -c core.autocrlf=false, npm ci) only in your own folder under <scratch> (the real path is in the message that launched you). Node 22 first on PATH (<node22>). A server you start binds port 0 or a free high port and is stopped by its exact process id; never bind, probe or stop the ports 4780, 4781, 4782 and 4790. One browser at a time on this PC. No git commit, push, pull, checkout, stash, reset or tag. LF line endings. Never write the name of the reference product, nor a path of this computer, into a Sai file or a handoff (write <scratch> or <outside the project>). Fill only the result of your handoff; the top-level status stays PENDING and completed_at null: ORCH closes. English.

F2, F3 (t5), F4 (read auth-mw.js, audit.js, audit-store.js), F5-F10 (t1, t2: the designer's trial migration applied through the real runner; audit then switch then insert commits together and rolls back together, forced RLS, composite key, version checks, insert-only trigger and purge setting, users guard, invite rule, widened checks, grants), F11 (t4), F12 and F13 (t3: consent word counts, lint after the exception, digests, KZ rows and 5 000 moments), F15, F16, F17, F18, F19, F20 (grep empty), F22 (t6) repeated or read; my own addition: unique (project_id, version) refuses a duplicate (23505), quick_facts must be an object (23514), a stage outside the list is refused (23514) (the designer's own line for the unique key was a syntax error in the sketch and measured nothing; the design does not claim it). Every claim held. The shared mechanisms checked for neighbouring places (AP-014): every tenant route takes the one switched transaction; every audit writer call stays under platform settings; the cleanup (auth-store.js) runs after the handler under whatever settings the request holds (N1). Pass B (developer): signatures, shapes, route table (14 rows, six meta keys), bodies, answers, codes (31), failure paths, files and owners are given in full and agree with the released code; no implementation code (types, tables, closed lists). Places where the developer would choose or be stopped: P1, P2, P3. Pass C (tests): 22 of 22 criteria have a design element and named tests (section 7, rows counted: REQ-116 10, REQ-117 12; the counts 79 new tests, 26+44+7+2 and the new-file counts 12/73 recomputed and equal); no «decide later» row. The consent sentences equal the REQ text character for character and every fixed phrase of criterion 5 stands in them (read); the narrow exception is the one REQ-111 criterion 3 as amended asks (strip the exact phrase once, in five keys at most; F12 shows exactly one Ц form per language and nothing else). Pass D (checkers): Q1-Q14 and R1-R3 are named with how or why not; no contradiction with decisions/0100, 0127, 0133-0138 or the released code (decisions/0137 Addition 4: the writer stays platform-only; the plan hook is the answer of 0138 C1). Protection in the same operation: the plan reads and locks under platform settings with an explicit organisation filter, the audit row is appended before the switch and the action runs under forced row security in the same transaction (measured and re-run with the real writer, t9: killed M1-M4); the invite is spent by one conditional update after every check and committed with the user, consent record, membership, organisation, used_by and audit row (t9 accept model: every refusal of criterion 2 leaves counts and the invite row unchanged); the version number is read under the project row lock (PGlite serialises, so only the pg job proves it, named); the purge setting is transaction-local and set and cleared inside one store function (residual named, N5); deletion is one transaction. Replacement table G1-G26 checked line by line against app/test and tools/test on the clone: 25 rows are exact (the lines named exist as stated: route-table 206/208/281-298/14, texts 1566/1596, isolation 629/520/575/634/645/798, permission-matrix 117, auth-session 316, rate-limit 232/317, rls 90/49, migrate 290, npmrc lists 26/6/2, public-pages, public-build, vercel-build page lists, fixtures/auth.js TABLES 13). One guard is missing: RA-5 of auth-reauth.test.js (P1). The sub-step red lists were checked the same way: B2 omits RLS-2 and RLS-3 (P2); B3 and B1 are right (SS-9 stays green until B5 because me() maps its fields). Mutants applied (25, on sketches built from the design text, original passes every expectation): M1, M2, M3, M4 (the pipeline: TP-1, TP-2, TP-5, PRJ-1); M25, M26, M27, M42, trigger TRUNCATE dropped, users guard dropped (RLS-6, RLS-2, DEL-7, OO-3); M43, M44, M45, M46, M47, M48, M50, M55, M56, M60 (the accept, INV-4 and INV-5); M33, M34 (STG-2 over 121 pairs); M38, M39, M40 (KZ-1). All killed; M44 is killed by INV-4 (used_at and used_by) and NOT by INV-5 or INV-6 as the design names them (N2). M18 and M52-type row-lock mutants need Postgres: only the pg job can show them, as the design says. Sub-steps B1-B7, F1-F4, T1-T5: order sound (contract, store, service, routes; F after B1; T last); B5 (six route files) and F4 (ten pages and scripts) are each too large to check alone (N6). Verdict FAIL for three small blocking edits of the design (P1, P2, P3); everything else passes. A short pass 2 on those sections is enough.

findings.place: §9 G2 (auth-reauth.test.js), §10 B5, REQ-117 criterion 12 «no other test changes»
findings.text: RA-5 of app/test/int/auth-reauth.test.js (lines 225-290) reads the real route table, takes every route with `meta.reauth` not null and asserts `CASES[key]` exists («no case for …»). After this work the table holds POST /api/admin/invites (owner_identity) and POST /api/admin/users/:id/delete (user_delete), so RA-5 turns red with no case for either. G2 names only the `PURPOSES` list of the same file. Needed: a row (or an extension of G2) saying RA-5's CASES gains the two routes (a canonical body each; the delete case needs a throwaway user), and RA-5 in B5's list of red tests.

pg/rls.test.js RLS-2 (lines 228-262) and RLS-3 (line 358) read the tenant tables from information_schema and assert that every listed table has rows of each of the three organisations («a table without its fixture rows fails here»). 0003 adds projects and idea_versions, so both turn red at B2 as soon as the migration exists; the fixture() of that file must insert their rows. G12 has the change, but B2's list of red tests names only MG-1, MG-6 and RLS-5, and §10 says a red test not in the row is a stop for the developer. Needed: RLS-2 and RLS-3 (and the fixture) in B2's red list.

Step 9a writes the audit entry as `{ orgId: session.orgId, actorKind, actorId, ip, …planned.audit }`: the plan's keys come last, so a plan that sets orgId or actorKind would overwrite the session's values, against «never the plan's». TP-5 demands that such a plan makes the request fail (TypeError, rolled back), but appendAudit's own check ignores unknown keys, so nothing in the written rule produces that failure. Measured on a pipeline sketch with the real writer (t9): with the formula as written the row of another organisation is written (M3: «rows of B 1», request committed); copying exactly four keys without a check also fails TP-5. Needed: state that the pipeline builds the entry from the session first, takes exactly action, targetKind, targetId and details from the plan, and throws TypeError on any other key, before any statement.

The lazy cleanup runs at step 12 under the settings the handler left; on a tenant route that is tenant settings, so the new `delete from invites …` is filtered by row security to the caller's organisation and never sees the null-organisation invites of a new client (harmless: every platform request cleans them). RL-5's case for stale invites must reach the cleanup through a platform route; say so.

M44 (the accept never claims the invite) is named as caught by INV-5 and INV-6. Measured on the accept model (t9): a second accept of the same code fails as account_exists (the e-mail now has an account), so INV-6 still sees exactly one 200 and INV-5's used-code case sees a refusal with unchanged counts; only INV-4's check that used_at and used_by are set kills it. Name INV-4, and let the INV-5 used-code case assert the answer `not_found` and a code planted as used without an account.

shownTextFindings (the shown-text lint of the browser kit) applies lintText with no exception to the whole visible text. If ACC-1 or the UAT step calls it on invite.html with the consent sentences filled in, the fifth sentence is a finding (list Ц «дней»/«days»). Say that those runs read the consent elements through the exception (or skip #consent-1…5 in that lint).

Deleting an org_owner of a customer organisation that keeps other members leaves the organisation without an owner (approvals of M3/M4 are for org_owner only). V1 invites make this rare; name it as accepted or as a question for M3.

Anything that can run SQL as sai_app can set app.purge_org to its own organisation and delete that organisation's idea versions (it cannot touch another organisation's, measured E4). The design names this residual and Q9 closes the SQL-injection path. A stronger form, for a later hardening: no DELETE grant on idea_versions and projects for sai_app and a SECURITY DEFINER purge function owned by the migration role.

B5 (invites, projects, admin-projects, admin and auth routes and the table) turns about ten test groups red at once and F4 builds ten pages and scripts: neither can be checked alone. Suggest B5a (invites, deletion), B5b (projects with the plan), B5c (admin board, card, audit) and F4a (client pages) and F4b (admin pages).

Wording: «the plan wrote nothing» (4.4 facts) while planCreate increments the daily quota (a write that rolls back with a refusal); and B1's red-test note says «F1's texts» where F2 (texts.js) is meant.
